reasoning: A hybrid approach is chosen to balance deep feature-level reasoning with quantitative evidence from explainability tools. Autonomous analysis helps identify candidate features through cross-instance comparisons, while XAI tools provide objective attribution scores to validate spurious influence. This combination increases confidence in identifying truly shared and semantically irrelevant features driving misclassification.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 47835) and which are unique to each instance.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of common features shared across all three instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, age, occupation) is semantically related to income class or if it might be a spurious correlation due to co-occurrence with other factors.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A justification of which shared features are likely spurious and not meaningfully related to income prediction

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP and Integrated Gradients provide consistent per-feature attribution scores across instances, enabling detection of shared high-impact features. LIME adds local interpretability, verifying feature importance in specific misclassified cases. Sensitivity analysis confirms feature impact by ablation, helping distinguish spurious from meaningful signals. Using all tools together increases robustness in identifying features that are both shared and non-semantic.
